title: Ex 2.5 #11 · R and S when P is false
prompt: Suppose $P$ is false and the statement $(R \Rightarrow S) \Leftrightarrow (P \wedge Q)$ is true. Find the truth values of $R$ and $S$. You can reason this out without a full truth table.
answer_format: Truth values for R and S, like R = T, S = F.
hints: With P false, what is the truth value of P ∧ Q, whatever Q is?
A ⇔ statement is true only when both sides have the same truth value. When is an implication R ⇒ S false?
solution: Since $P$ is false, $P \wedge Q$ is false no matter what $Q$ is.
The biconditional is true, so both of its sides match: $R \Rightarrow S$ is false as well.
An implication is false only when its hypothesis is true and its conclusion is false, so $R$ is true and $S$ is false.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the truth tables for ∧, ∨, ∼, ⇒ and ⇔ (Sections 2.2–2.5).

submission.answer: P = F, Q = T, R = T, S = F
P = F, Q = F, R = F, S = F
